item.description: In Reply We thank Dr Wu and colleagues for their interest in our article. The random-effects model demonstrated consistent results—this was a prespecified sensitivity analysis and can be found in eFigure 12 in Supplement 1 of the article. The overall point estimates and the uncertainty intervals were largely unchanged with random-effects compared with fixed-effects models. We chose to use fixed-effects models as the primary analysis because of the errors random-effects models are prone to, with potential undue influence of small studies.
